title: Provider capability and authentication secrecy
summary: Provider credentials and resumable-session capabilities are operational secrets, not Storage object identity. Common Storage evidence records stable identities and offsets while secret-bearing provider state remains transient or behind provider-private secure authority.
invariants: Authorization bearer tokens never belong in StorageRef, catalogue, planner evidence, generic checkpoint or logs.
A resumable upload session URI is bearer-like capability material and receives the same secrecy treatment as a credential.
Generic transfer restart evidence stores stable sink identity and byte offset, not the secret session URI.
If production restart requires preserving a provider capability, persist it behind provider-private secure authority rather than weakening common Storage persistence.
Authentication leases should be short-lived and retired after each request; Secret Broker remains the credential-authority seam.

provenance.claim: Code separates auth leases and provider session capabilities from generic Storage persistence.
Regression inspects persisted checkpoint slots and rejects leakage of bearer token or resumable-session capability.
